earlier_scan.source_named: North Picene: extinct, unclassifiable, essentially one undeciphered inscription (Novilara stele); no stress description exists.

new_statements.quote: Vanno ricordati, inoltre, i tentativi di riconoscere nel testo una struttura metrica, operati da W. Brandenstein (Brandenstein 1941) e da J.W. Poultney (Poultney 1979). Mentre il primo ha rintracciato, in modo a dire il vero poco sistematico, una scansione metrica del testo in asclepiadei, lo studioso americano ha proposto di riconoscere "a series of six trochaic tetrameters catalectic based on word-initial stress with syllabic quantities ignored". Attraverso una lettura del testo guidata da questo metro, egli arriva ad una divisione delle parole sostanzialmente identica con quanto proposto più sopra, tranne che nel caso di kalatne e niś, mantenute distinte.
new_statements.translation: Also to be recalled are the attempts to recognise a metrical structure in the text, made by W. Brandenstein (1941) and J.W. Poultney (1979). While the former traced, in a frankly unsystematic way, a metrical scansion of the text in asclepiads, the American scholar proposed recognising "a series of six trochaic tetrameters catalectic based on word-initial stress with syllabic quantities ignored". Reading the text guided by this metre, he arrives at a word division essentially identical to the one proposed above, except for kalatne and niś, which he keeps separate.
new_statements.citation: Di Carlo, Pierpaolo (2006). L'enigma nord-piceno. Saggio sulla lingua delle stele di Novilara e sul loro contesto culturale. Firenze: Dipartimento di Linguistica, Università di Firenze (Quaderni del Dipartimento di Linguistica, Studi 7). p. 29, §3.1.1 'Confini tra parole' — reporting Poultney, James W. (1979), The Language of the Northern Picene Inscriptions, JIES 7: 49-64.
new_statements.locator: p. 29 (running head 'Analisi morfologica 29'), §3.1.1 Confini tra parole
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (288,824 bytes; text layer of the Wayback copy of the author's academia.edu page for Di Carlo 2006, L'enigma nord-piceno). The passage is at extract lines 1382-1389, under the running head "Analisi morfologica 29" and section heading "3.1.1. Confini tra parole" (line 1343), exactly as the reader located it. The Italian text matches the reported quote word for word, including Poultney's embedded English "a series of six trochaic tetrameters catalectic based on word-initial stress with syllabic quantities ignored" and the closing clause "tranne che nel caso di kalatne e niś, mantenute distinte"; the only surface differences are a line-break hyphenation "rico-/noscere" in the text layer…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No description of North Picene stress exists. The only stress claim in the literature is Poultney's (1979) conjecture, reported by Di Carlo, that the longest Novilara inscription (PID 343) scans as trochaic tetrameters if every word is stressed on its initial syllable and vowel quantity is ignored; i.e. word-initial stress assumed as a metrical premise, not observed.
new_statements.exceptions: None; Brandenstein 1941 instead scanned the same text as quantitative asclepiads, which presupposes a different (quantity-based) prosody, so the two metrical readings are incompatible.
new_statements.domain_note: Applies to one untranslated 12-line inscription (about 60 words) in an unclassified language; the corpus has been argued to be a 19th-century forgery (Belfiore, Lugli & Naso 2021, per Wikipedia). Di Carlo's own phonology chapter (pp. 13-25) does not treat accent. This is a metrical hypothesis, not a phonological description, and should not enter the catalog as a stress rule.
new_statements.identity_note: North Picene = the language of the Novilara stelae (PID 343 long inscription, PID 344 fragment), central Adriatic Italy (Glottolog's country 'ES' is wrong; it is IT). Not related to South Picene (sabe1248 / Old Sabellic). The corpus is untranslated and has been argued to be a 19th-century forgery (Belfiore, Lugli & Naso 2021).

sources.note: Ch. 2 'Analisi fonologica' (pp. 13-25: inventory, stops/omicron, sibilants, palaeographic incongruities) says nothing about accent or stress. The only stress mention is p. 29 (§3.1.1 Confini tra parole), where Di Carlo reports Poultney 1979's metrical hypothesis for PID 343: 'a series of six trochaic tetrameters catalectic based on word-initial stress with syllabic quantities ignored', used only for word division; he does not endorse it.
